page_or_component: Home page main navigation dropdowns (About Us / Passport Offices / Services / Useful Links / Contact Us)
evidence: screenshots/web-001.png: Lighthouse flags [aria-*] attributes do not match their roles. Menu items are <a> tags with no href and aria-expanded, and all five share the same id collasible-nav-dropdown3. Keyboard pass: Tab goes Search > Login > Register > View More, skipping every menu item
user_impact: Keyboard-only users cannot open any menu section. Screen reader users are not told these are expandable menus
recommended_fix: Replace each <a> with <button type="button" aria-expanded="false">, toggle aria-expanded on open, give each a unique id

evidence: screenshots/web-002.png: Lighthouse flags Buttons do not have an accessible name. <button class="menu-btn"> has no text or aria-label
user_impact: Screen readers announce only "button", so blind users cannot tell this button opens the site menu
recommended_fix: Add aria-label="Open menu" and aria-expanded that reflects the menu state

page_or_component: Home page announcements and circulars carousels
wcag_reference: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 2.4.4 Link Purpose; 2.4.7 Focus Visible
evidence: screenshots/web-003.png: Lighthouse flags [aria-hidden="true"] elements contain focusable descendants. 80+ hidden slides (including cloned slides) contain focusable Know More links, all with identical link text. Keyboard pass: after 15+ Tabs focus was still in circulars and the focus box vanished onto off-screen slides
user_impact: Keyboard users Tab into links on slides they cannot see. Screen reader users land on links that are hidden from them, and every link is announced only as "Know More" with no context
recommended_fix: Add tabindex="-1" to links inside hidden slides (or use inert), and give each link a descriptive name, e.g. "Know more about Tatkaal Passport"

page_or_component: Images across the home page (emblem logo / service cards / chatbot button / phone icons)
evidence: screenshots/web-004.png: Lighthouse flags Image elements do not have [alt] attributes on 23 images, including the national emblem logo, 8 service card images and the chatbot image that acts as a button
user_impact: Screen readers read out file names or nothing. The chatbot image works as a button but has no name, so blind users cannot find or use the chatbot
recommended_fix: Add meaningful alt to informative images (alt="Government of India emblem"), alt="" to decorative ones (stars, phone icons), and turn the chatbot image into a <button> with aria-label="Open chat assistant"
